title: Throughput Beacon: deterministic certification harness and acceptance checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Build a compact, deterministic certification harness ("Throughput Beacon") that teams and customers can run to validate dedicated capacity offerings against advertised throughput and tail-latency guarantees. The Beacon is intended for final pre-production signoff and for customers to run during Dedicated onboarding.

Scope: single-tenant and shared-tenant modes, warm and cold KV-cache baselines, three workload profiles (short-chat, long-context generation, embedding-batch), optional prefix caching enabled/disabled, and quantized model variants. The harness must produce machine-readable artifacts: a signed result bundle + human-readable checklist.

Goals: provide repeatable measurements with low variance (<= 3% TPS across 5 consecutive runs), clear pass/fail rules for committed throughput, deterministic artifact generation for automated gating, and a minimal footprint runnable in customer test environments (requires only a single client or low-footprint controller).
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic run: consecutive runs on same infra show <= 3% TPS variance for each workload profile
SLO validation: 99th-tail latency for committed throughput must be below runtime-2.4 SLA thresholds in >= 95% of runs
Recovery: simulated node failure and autoscaler intervention must restore capacity to target throughput within 60s without exceeding error rate thresholds
Artifacts: harness emits JSON report, CSV time-series, and an HTML checklist with per-metric explanations
Onboarding: runbook and customer checklist reviewed and approved by Solutions Eng and QA
notes_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting — agreed to avoid heavy 'replay' approach; use trace resynthesis + parametric workload generators to keep tests lightweight for customers.
2026-03-11: Experimented with KV-cache warmup heuristics; found 10k token priming reduces cold-start variance by ~18% for long-context profile (see perf dash).
2026-03-12: Design decision: output bundle will be signed with customer key for non-repudiation; added dependency on infra PR for key handling (see github link).
Next steps: finalize controller CLI, add CI job to run Beacon on canary fleet weekly, draft customer-facing Confluence checklist.
test_plan_summary: Testbed: small dedicated cluster (4x A100 equivalent) and a lightweight controller image. Metrics collected: QPS, tokens/s, 50/95/99/99.9 latencies, error rates, memory/GPU utilization, cost estimate per-1000 tokens. Methodology: run fixed-duration ramp-sustain sweeps across target throughput points (50%, 75%, 100%, 110% of commit), collect 6 independent runs per point, and compute median + interquartile variance. Failure injection: random instance termination during sustain window to validate autoscaling and graceful degradation. Report generation: JUnit-style summary + signed artifacts.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: prototype controller + workload generator (2w). Phase 2: integrate signed artifact generation, CI integration, and failure-injection hooks (1w). Phase 3: customer docs, Solutions Eng walkthrough, enable on canary fleet (1w). Owner: Miguel Ortega. QA: Priya Raman. Solutions Eng review: Lars Nystrom.
risks_and_mitigations: Variance from noisy shared infra — mitigation: recommend dedicated-seat execution or short warmup windows, and include gating to require single-tenant run for final signoff.
False positives from ephemeral autoscaler throttles — mitigation: inject controlled delays and track autoscaler signals to correlate incidents.
Customer environment heterogeneity — mitigation: provide minimal required specs and a lightweight Dockerized controller to standardize runs.
